title: In situ TEM of Biological Assemblies in Liquid
protocol: Clean silicon nitride E-chips by incubating them in 15 ml of acetone for 2 minutes.
Incubate the chips in 15 ml of methanol for 2 minutes.
Allow chips to dry under laminar air-flow.
Incubate dried chips on a heated stir plate at 150 °C for 1.5 hours without stirring.
Cool chips to room temperature before use.
Compose lipid mixtures using Hamilton syringes in small glass tubes containing 25% chloroform, 55% DLPC (1 mg/ml) and 20% Ni-NTA lipid (1 mg/ml).
Apply a 1 μl aliquot of the mixture over each 15 μl drop of Milli-Q water on Parafilm in a humid Petri dish.
Incubate samples on ice for at least 60 minutes.
Place an E-chip with a 150 nm integrated spacer on top of a monolayer sample and incubate for 1 minute.
Gently lift the chip off of the sample.
Add a 3 μl aliquot of His-tagged Protein A to the chip.
Incubate the chip with His-tagged Protein A for 1 minute at room temperature.
Blot away excess drop using Whatman #1 filter paper.
Immediately add a 3 μl aliquot of antibody solution to the chip.
Incubate the chip with antibody solution for 1 minute at room temperature.
Remove excess solution using a Hamilton syringe.
Add a 1 μl aliquot of rotavirus DLPs (0.1 mg/ml) in buffer solution containing 50 mM HEPES (pH 7.5), 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2 and 10 mM CaCl2.
Incubate for at least 2 min at room temperature.
Load the wet E-chip containing the viral sample into the tip of the microfluidic specimen holder.
Glow-discharge a second flat E-chip for 1 min then load it on top of the spacer chip.
Alternatively, add heavy metal stain (e.g., 0.2% uranyl formate) to wet specimens prior to placing the second E-chip on the wet specimen.
Wash the E-chip containing the specimen with Milli-Q water if a contrast reagent is added.
Sandwich the entire assembly together to form a sealed enclosure, held in place mechanically within the holder by 3 brass screws.
Pump the tip of the holder to 10-6 Torr using a turbo-pumped dry pumping station before placing the holder inside the TEM.
Load the in situ specimen holder into a Transmission Electron Microscope equipped with a LaB6 filament and operating at 120 kV.
Turn on the TEM filament.
Adjust the eucentric height of the microscope stage using the wobbler function by tilting the sample from -15° to +15° back and forth in the column.
Record images along the edges and in the corner regions of the microfluidic chamber first.
Record images of specimens under low-dose conditions (1-3 electrons/Å2) using a CCD camera.
Use nominal magnifications of 6,000X - 30,000X.
Determine the proper defocus value by focusing at the edge of the fluidic chamber.
Use a defocus value of -1.5 μm to record images at 30,000X magnification.
If thick solution is encountered or if contrast agent is not used in specimen preparation, use higher defocus values in the range of -2 to -4 μm.
Focus the electron beam until bubbles are formed in the liquid within the device.
